Adapter + ContractCreationHandler template

Implement PaymentAdapterInterface.
Extend ContractCreationHandler. That’s the spine.

1. Adapter — bridge the PSP SDK
class StripeAdapter implements PaymentAdapterInterface
{
    public function createPayment(
        CreatePaymentRequest $req
    ): PaymentResponse {
        $pi = $this->stripe->paymentIntents->create([
            'amount'   => $this->toCents($req->getAmount()),
            'currency' => strtolower($req->getCurrency()),
            'metadata' => $req->getMetadata(),
        ]);
        return new PaymentResponse(
            providerPaymentId: $pi->id,
            status: $this->mapStatus($pi->status),
            amount: $req->getAmount(),
            currency: $req->getCurrency(),
            requiresAction: $pi->status === 'requires_action',
            clientSecret: $pi->client_secret,
        );
    }
    // capture / refund / authorize / void / 3DS / vault …
}
2. Template-method handler
class StripeContractCreationHandler
    extends ContractCreationHandler
{
    protected function afterContractCreated(
        PaymentContractInterface $c,
        EventContextInterface $ctx
    ): void {
        $c->setMetadata('payment_method', $this->methodFrom($ctx));
        $ctx->set('contractId', $c->getId());
    }
    // Base class handles repo save + event dispatch.
}

services.yaml · tagged iterator
StripeContractCreationHandler:
    tags:
      - { name: payment.event_handler, priority: 100 }

EventListenerProviderInterface:
    class: EventListenerProvider
    arguments:
      - !tagged_iterator payment.event_handler
Adding a whole new PSP requires zero modifications to payment-component. A new adapter, a new factory, a new ContractCreationHandler subclass, register in services.yaml. The core stays untouched — that’s the SOLID Open/Closed promise.
